content.value_statement: AI-generated interfaces often look generic or miss production details. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code strict design and frontend guardrails.
actual_capabilities: Checks dependency use against package.json before suggesting UI libraries.
Enforces React and Next.js component boundaries for interactive UI.
Guides Tailwind CSS layout, typography, spacing, and color choices.
Adds loading, empty, error, and active interaction states.
Directs motion work toward transform, opacity, and isolated client components.
Provides a final checklist for responsive and performance issues.
limitations: Instruction-only skill; it does not include source components or templates.
Assumes React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, and common animation libraries unless the user says otherwise.
Some motion concepts require installed dependencies and project-specific performance review.
Strong visual rules may conflict with an existing brand system.

use_cases.title: Refine React Screens
use_cases.description: Improve a rough React or Next.js screen with clearer hierarchy, responsive layouts, and complete UI states.

use_cases.title: Set Visual Guardrails
use_cases.description: Apply strict rules for typography, color, spacing, and motion before an agent writes interface code.

use_cases.title: Ship Better Prototypes
use_cases.description: Turn a product idea into a polished prototype with practical design constraints and performance checks.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Single Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Use design-taste-frontend to improve this screen. Preserve the current stack. Focus on spacing, typography, color restraint, and mobile behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for visual cleanup on one page.

prompt_templates.title: Generate a Dashboard UI
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React dashboard for [product]. Use dense data layout rules, complete loading and empty states, and no generic card grid.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a production-style dashboard.

prompt_templates.title: Add Motion Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Add motion to this interface. Keep animations isolated in client components. Use transform and opacity only. Include cleanup for any effects.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for interaction design with performance limits.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Full Flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this multi-page frontend flow. Identify weak visual hierarchy, missing states, risky motion, and responsive issues before editing code.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert request for a design and implementation review.

output_examples.input: Improve a SaaS billing page that feels flat and generic.
output: A clearer information hierarchy with restrained color and sharper typography.
Responsive sections that avoid generic equal-card rows.
Loading, empty, error, and active states for billing actions.

output_examples.input: Create a product analytics dashboard with motion.
output: A dense dashboard layout using lines and spacing instead of excessive cards.
Motion guidance that uses transform and opacity for smoother performance.
A review checklist for mobile collapse, dependency use, and animation isolation.

best_practices: Share product context, target users, and existing brand constraints before asking for implementation.
Ask the agent to inspect package.json before adding any third-party UI or motion library.
Review mobile layouts and motion performance after each generated frontend change.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to override an existing design system without approval.
Do not request heavy perpetual animation for data-dense or low-power mobile workflows.
Do not accept new dependencies unless the project supports them or the team approves installation.

faq.question: Does this skill write frontend code?
faq.answer: It guides an AI agent while it writes or reviews frontend code. It does not ship components by itself.

faq.question: Which stacks does it target?
faq.answer: It favors React, Next.js, Tailwind CSS, and common motion libraries. The user can request a different stack.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The content is instruction based and lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. The skill is a Markdown instruction file. It may reference placeholder image URLs as examples.

faq.question: Will it install dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: No. It tells the agent to check package.json and show install commands when a package is missing.

faq.question: Is it safe for production projects?
faq.answer: It is suitable as guidance, but generated code still needs normal review, testing, and accessibility checks.
